questions.q: Using the 11-test, which number is divisible by 11: 8294, 7315, 6481 or 9053?
questions.explanation: 8294 gives alternating digit sum (8+9)-(2+4)=11, a multiple of 11.

questions.q: The product 18×24×25 expressed as 2^a×3^b×5^c has a+b+c equal to what?
questions.explanation: 18 supplies 2¹3², 24 supplies 2³3¹, and 25 supplies 5². Thus a=4, b=3, c=2, and the sum is 9.

questions.q: What is the remainder when 7^103 is divided by 24?
questions.explanation: Powers of 7 modulo 24 cycle 7,1 (7²=49≡1). Since 103 is odd, 7^103≡7.

questions.q: Three rods of lengths 84 cm, 126 cm and 210 cm are to be cut into equal whole-centimetre pieces without waste. What is the longest possible piece length?
questions.explanation: The longest common measure is HCF(84,126,210)=42 cm.

questions.q: Three warning lights flash every 18, 24 and 30 seconds. If they flash together at 10:00, when will they next do so?
questions.explanation: LCM(18,24,30)=360 seconds = 6 minutes.

questions.q: A number leaves remainder 4 on division by 9 and remainder 6 on division by 11. Which is the smallest positive such number?
questions.explanation: 94=9×10+4 and 94=11×8+6; smaller candidates below 94 do not satisfy both conditions.

questions.q: The product of three consecutive integers is always divisible by which least positive integer?
questions.explanation: Among three consecutive integers, one is divisible by 3 and at least one is even, so the product is divisible by 6.

questions.q: What is the value of 960÷(24×4)+18×3?
Which fraction lies between 5/8 and 7/10?
Which value is closest to 0.078×250?
A sum of ₹1,440 is divided in the ratio 5:3:2. What is the largest share?
questions.explanation: There are 10 parts, each ₹144, so the largest share is 5×144=₹720.

questions.q: If a:b=4:7 and b:c=3:5, what is a:c?
Four machines can manufacture 30 units in 18 hours. How many machines are needed to manufacture 50 units in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: Required machines =4×(50/30)×(18/12)=10.

questions.q: The cost of 13 identical pens is ₹195. What is the cost of 29 pens?
questions.explanation: Cost per pen is ₹195/13=₹15, so 29 pens cost ₹435.

questions.q: A map scale is 1:250,000. If two towns are 18 cm apart on the map, their real distance is:
A value increases by 10% and then decreases by 10%. The net result is:
questions.explanation: The multiplier is 1.10×0.90=0.99, which is a 1% decrease.

questions.q: A candidate scores 315 marks and falls 45 marks short of the pass mark. If the pass mark is 36%, what is the maximum mark?
questions.explanation: Pass mark =315+45=360; 36% of maximum is 360, so maximum=360×100/36=1000.

questions.q: An article costs ₹600 and is sold for ₹720 after a 20% trade discount. What was the marked price?
questions.explanation: Selling price is 80% of marked price: M×0.80=720, so M=₹900.

questions.q: A shopkeeper uses a 900 g weight instead of a 1 kg weight and marks goods 10% above cost. His net gain is:
questions.explanation: He sells 900 g as 1 kg and adds 10%, equivalent to 110/90=22.22% gain.

questions.q: A jacket marked ₹2,500 is sold at a 12% discount. The sale price is:
questions.explanation: 12% of ₹2,500 is ₹300, so sale price is ₹2,200.

questions.q: A town’s population rises from 40,000 to 44,100 in two years at a constant annual rate. The annual rate is:
questions.explanation: 44,100/40,000=(1.05)², so the constant annual rate is 5%.

questions.q: A 20% discount followed by a 10% discount is equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.explanation: The net multiplier is 0.80×0.90=0.72, hence 28%.

questions.q: A is 25% more than B. B is what percent less than A?
questions.explanation: If B=100, A=125; the difference is 25/125=20%.

questions.q: ₹7,200 earns ₹1,296 simple interest in 3 years. The annual rate is:
The compound interest on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum is:
questions.explanation: Amount=5000×1.1²=6050, so interest=1050.

questions.q: The average of 18 numbers is 32. What is their total sum?
The average weight of 20 students rises by 0.5 kg when one 52 kg student is replaced. The replacement student weighs:
questions.explanation: The total rises by 20×0.5=10 kg, so replacement weighs 52+10=62 kg.

questions.q: A 30-litre mixture has milk and water in 4:1. How much water must be added to make milk:water=2:1?
questions.explanation: Milk=24 L, water=6 L. For 24:(6+x)=2:1, 6+x=12, so x=6.

questions.q: How much 15% acid solution must be mixed with 4 litres of 35% acid solution to obtain 25% acid solution?
questions.explanation: At 25%, the two concentrations are equidistant, so equal quantities are needed: 4 L.

questions.q: The average marks of 40 boys and 60 girls is 72 and 68, respectively. The combined average is:
A 40-litre mixture has milk and water in 3:1. If 10 litres are removed and replaced with water, the new milk:water ratio is:
questions.explanation: The removed portion retains 3:1. Remaining milk=30-7.5=22.5 L and water=10-2.5=7.5 L; 10 L water is added, making 22.5:17.5=9:7.

questions.q: Two equal sums are invested for 2 years at 6% and 8% simple interest. The difference in interest is ₹160. What is each sum?
questions.explanation: Difference in annual rates is 2%; in 2 years difference=4% of sum. 4% of sum=160, so sum=4000.

questions.q: A completes a job in 15 days and B in 20 days. Together they finish in:
questions.explanation: Combined rate=1/15+1/20=7/60 job/day, time=60/7≈8.57 days.

questions.q: A is 25% more efficient than B. If B takes 30 days, A takes:
questions.explanation: A’s rate is 1.25 times B, so time is 30/1.25=24 days.

questions.q: A and B complete 2/5 of a job together in 6 days. C alone completes the remaining 3/5 in 9 days. How long would C alone take for the whole job?
questions.explanation: C’s 3/5 work takes 9 days, so full work takes 9×5/3=15 days.

questions.q: An inlet fills a tank in 12 hours and an outlet empties it in 18 hours. Both open together fill it in:
questions.explanation: Net rate=1/12-1/18=1/36 tank/hour.

questions.q: A 180 m train crosses a pole in 12 seconds. Its speed is:
A 120 m train at 54 km/h passes a 180 m train moving opposite at 36 km/h. Crossing time is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed=(54+36)×5/18=25 m/s; total length=300 m; time=12 s.

questions.q: A boat has downstream speed 18 km/h and upstream speed 10 km/h. Its speed in still water is:
questions.explanation: Still-water speed=(18+10)/2=14 km/h.

questions.q: A runner covers 7.2 km in 48 minutes. The speed in km/h is:
questions.explanation: 48 minutes=0.8 hour, so speed=7.2/0.8=9 km/h.

questions.q: In a 100 m race, A finishes 10 m ahead of B. A and C finish simultaneously in a race whose length is 100 m when C is 20 m behind A. By what distance does B lead C at A’s finish?
questions.explanation: For the same A-time: B covers 90 m while C covers 80 m, so B is 10 m ahead of C when A finishes.

questions.q: A vehicle travels 60 km at 30 km/h and 60 km at 60 km/h. Its average speed for the whole trip is:
questions.explanation: Total time=60/30+60/60=3 hours; total distance=120 km; average=40 km/h.

questions.q: If 5x-17=43, what is x?
questions.explanation: 5x=60, hence x=12.

questions.q: If x+y=19 and x-y=7, what is xy?
The roots of x²-11x+28=0 are:
questions.explanation: The equation factors as (x-4)(x-7)=0.

questions.q: For real and distinct roots, the discriminant of 2x²+px-3=0 must satisfy:
questions.explanation: Discriminant=p²-4×2×(-3)=p²+24, always positive for real p.

questions.q: The value of (√48+√27)/√3 is:
questions.explanation: √48=4√3 and √27=3√3, so sum=7√3; dividing by √3 gives 7.

questions.q: The value of 2^5×8^-1 is:
If x+1/x=6, then x²+1/x² is:
questions.explanation: Square both sides: x²+2+1/x²=36, hence x²+1/x²=34.

questions.q: The 15th term of the AP 7,11,15,... is:
The sum of the first 25 odd positive integers is:
questions.explanation: The sum of first n odd integers is n²=625.

questions.q: The 6th term of the sequence 5,15,45,... is:
questions.explanation: The ratio is 3; T6=5×3^5=1215.

questions.q: A rectangular garden is 14 m by 9 m. Its area is:
A circle has circumference 88 cm. Using π=22/7, its radius is:
A sector has radius 12 cm and central angle 60°. Its sector area is:
A cuboid 8 cm×5 cm×3 cm has volume:
questions.explanation: Volume=8×5×3=120 cm³.

questions.q: A cube has edge 6 cm. Its total surface area is:
questions.explanation: Total surface area=6×6²=216 cm².

questions.q: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Using π=22/7, its curved surface area is:
Two angles of a triangle are 48° and 67°. The third angle is:
questions.explanation: The sum of angles is 180°, so third=180-48-67=65°.

questions.q: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. Its hypotenuse is:
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse=√(9²+12²)=√225=15 cm.

questions.q: A cone has radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm. Its height is:
A square of side 11 cm is enlarged so that each side becomes 22 cm. Its area becomes how many times the original?
questions.explanation: Area scales with the square of side ratio: 2²=4.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of a prime number?
questions.explanation: Prime faces are 2,3,5: 3 out of 6.

questions.q: A card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. Probability of a red king is:
questions.explanation: There are 2 red kings among 52 cards, giving 2/52=1/26.

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed twice. Probability of exactly one head is:
questions.explanation: The outcomes HT and TH are 2 of 4 equally likely outcomes.

questions.q: How many four-letter arrangements can be made from 7 distinct letters without repetition?
How many different teams of 3 can be chosen from 8 people?
A committee of 3 is chosen from 6 men and 4 women, with at least 2 men. How many committees qualify?
questions.explanation: Exactly 2 men: C(6,2)×C(4,1)=60; exactly 3 men=C(6,3)=20; total=80.

questions.q: The median of 7,3,12,9,5,11,8 is:
questions.explanation: The sorted data is 3,5,7,8,9,11,12; the middle value is 8.

questions.q: Two groups contain 20 and 30 observations with means 75 and 65. The combined mean is:
The range of 18,42,31,27,55 is:
questions.explanation: Maximum 55 minus minimum 18 is 37.

questions.q: What is the average of p and q? I: p+q=30. II: p-q=6.
questions.explanation: I directly gives (p+q)/2=15. II alone does not provide the sum.

questions.q: A table shows 240, 300, 270 and 330 units sold in weeks 1 to 4. Total sales are:
A bar chart shows production 180 tonnes in 2023 and 225 tonnes in 2024. The percentage increase is:
Monthly exports are 18,22,20,24 and 26 crore. The average is:
questions.explanation: Sum=110 crore over 5 months; average=22 crore.

questions.q: A sector representing 18% of a pie chart has central angle:
A library bought 160 books: 45% fiction, 25% reference, and the rest biography. How many biographies were bought?
questions.explanation: Remaining percentage=30%, and 30% of 160=48.

questions.q: A table lists males:females as 420:280. The simplified ratio is:
questions.explanation: Divide 420:280 by 140 to get 3:2.

questions.q: Two branches record first-quarter sales of 180 and 200 and second-quarter sales of 216 and 240. Which is true?
A pie chart allocates 45°, 90°, 135° and 90° to four products. The 45° product represents:
In a 500-person survey, 180 prefer A, 125 prefer B and 195 prefer C. The mode is:
questions.explanation: C has the largest frequency, 195.

questions.q: Watch is to time as thermometer is to:
questions.explanation: A watch measures time, and a thermometer measures temperature/heat.

questions.q: Which is the odd one out: 16,36,64,81?
questions.explanation: 16,36 and64 are even perfect squares;81 is odd.

questions.q: What comes next: 3,8,15,24,35,...?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5,7,9,11, then13; 35+13=48.

questions.q: What comes next: 2A,6D,12G,20J,...?
questions.explanation: Multipliers are 1×2,2×3,3×4,4×5, while letters advance by3; next 30M.

questions.q: What comes next: A3, D6, G12, J24,...?
questions.explanation: Letters advance by3 and numbers double each term.

questions.q: Find the missing term: 13,21,29,__,45,53.
questions.explanation: The sequence adds8 consistently.

questions.q: Which letter comes next: C,F,J,O,__?
questions.explanation: Alphabet positions advance by 3,4,5,6: C(3)→F(6)→J(10)→O(15)→U(21).

questions.q: Nucleus is to cell as engine is to:
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the controlling central part of a cell; the engine is a central power source for a vehicle.

questions.q: If ORBIT is coded by adding 2 to each letter, the code is:
questions.explanation: O→Q,R→T,B→D,I→K,T→V: QTDKV.

questions.q: In a code, a 3-digit number is doubled and its digit sum is added. Thus 214 becomes 428+7=435. What does 325 become?
If every letter of LAMP is moved one place forward in the alphabet, the code is:
questions.explanation: L→M,A→B,M→N,P→Q, giving MBNQ.

questions.q: P is the brother of Q. Q is the mother of R. How is P related to R?
questions.explanation: P is Q’s brother, and Q is R’s mother, so P is R’s maternal uncle.

questions.q: A says, “B is my mother’s only son.” If A is female, how is B related to A?
questions.explanation: A’s mother’s only son is A’s brother, assuming A has no other male sibling by that description.

questions.q: Starting east, a person turns right, then left, then left. The final facing direction is:
questions.explanation: Right from east→south, left→east, left→north.

questions.q: A walks 5 km north, 12 km east, then 5 km south. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: North and south cancel; remaining horizontal displacement is 12 km east.

questions.q: In a 31-runner race, a runner is 12th from the front. The rank from the back is:
Five boxes are stacked top to bottom. C is above D. A is below D. B is immediately above C. E is at the bottom. Which is third from top?
questions.explanation: Bottom upward: E,A,D,C,B. Third from top is C.

questions.q: Six people P,Q,R,S,T,U sit in a row. P is left of R but right of Q. S is left of Q. T is at an end. U is immediately right of R. Which is the correct order?
questions.explanation: Conditions give Q-P-R-U block and S left of Q; T must occupy the remaining end.

questions.q: Four friends are around a table. X sits opposite Y. Z is to the left of X. What is the position of W?
questions.explanation: If X north, Y south, Z west, W is east and opposite Z.

questions.q: In a 4-floor building, A lives below C; D lives immediately below C; B lives on the ground floor. Who is on the top?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: B,A,D,C, so C is top.

questions.q: All lilies are flowers. All flowers need sunlight. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
questions.explanation: The universal chain lilies→flowers→sunlight makes the conclusion necessary.

questions.q: Some artists are engineers. All engineers use diagrams. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
questions.explanation: For the engineers who are artists, if they are engineers they use diagrams.

questions.q: A city council restricted parking in one market area. Which conclusion is most strongly supported?
options: Traffic congestion was absent in that area
The council intended to change parking conditions
questions.explanation: The action itself supports a change in local parking conditions, not the other claims.

questions.q: “Carry a raincoat today; the forecast predicts heavy rain.” Which is an assumption?
options: It is impossible to carry umbrellas
questions.explanation: The recommendation presumes the forecast is sufficiently reliable.

questions.q: Argument: Online exams reduce travel cost. Should they replace all campus exams?
options: Yes, because all campus exams waste travel
No, a course still needs to consider security and practical assessment
Yes, because internet access is universal
No, because travel cost never matters
questions.explanation: The fact about cost is relevant but does not answer all suitability questions.

questions.q: Several visitors slipped near a museum entrance after rain. What action is most suitable?
options: Post a warning and use non-slip mats
questions.explanation: This directly reduces the immediate hazard while keeping access open.

questions.q: The company introduced split shifts. Absenteeism fell in the following quarter. What is most reasonable?
options: Split shifts necessarily caused lower absenteeism
The shift change may have contributed, but causation needs more evidence
questions.explanation: Temporal association is not proof of causation.

questions.q: Assertion: A square has four equal sides. Reason: A rectangle has four equal angles. Which is correct?
options: Both true and reason explains assertion
Both true but reason does not explain assertion
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but equal angles do not explain equal sides.

questions.q: All pilots are trained. Some trained people are doctors. Which diagram conclusion is certain?
questions.explanation: Every pilot is trained, so the set of trained people necessarily contains pilots.

questions.q: A leap year has 366 days. Which day of the week repeats 53 times if a leap year begins on Friday?
questions.explanation: A 366-day year has 52 weeks plus 2 days. The starting Friday and following Saturday occur 53 times.

questions.q: At 3:30, the angle between the minute and hour hands is:
questions.explanation: At 3:30, hour hand is 105° and minute hand 180°, difference75°.

questions.q: How often do the minute and hour hands overlap in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: Overlaps occur approximately every 65.45 minutes, 11 times in a 12-hour cycle.

questions.q: If 1 January is Monday, 1 February in a 31-day January is:
questions.explanation: 31 days is 3 days beyond a week; Monday+3=Thursday.

questions.q: If + means division and × means addition, what is 18+3×4 under the substitutions?
questions.explanation: 18÷3=6 and 4 means? + means division and × means addition, expression 18+3×4 becomes 18÷3+4=10.

questions.q: If A means +, B means ×, C means − and D means ÷, evaluate 20 D 5 B 3 C 2 A 7.
Can the value of x be uniquely determined? I: x is positive. II: x²=81.
questions.explanation: II gives x=±9 and I eliminates −9, leaving x=9.

questions.q: Is y divisible by 6? I: y is divisible by 3. II: y is even.
questions.explanation: Divisibility by 6 requires both 2 and 3.

questions.q: What is R’s rank from the left? I: R is 8th from the right. II: The row has 25 people.
questions.explanation: Both are needed: 25-8+1=18th from left.

questions.q: A task starts at 9:20 and lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. It finishes at:
Train A departs at 8:00 and every 20 minutes. Train B departs at 8:10 and every 25 minutes. The first common departure after 8:00 is:
questions.explanation: A departures include 9:00; B departures include 8:10,8:35,9:00, so 9:00 is first common.

questions.q: Meetings are scheduled Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Accounts is before HR, and HR is before Training. Which meeting is on Monday?
questions.explanation: The only complete order is Accounts→HR→Training, matching Monday→Wednesday→Friday.

questions.q: Exactly one of A, B and C is guilty. A says, “B is guilty.” B says, “A is guilty.” C says, “I am innocent.” If only A is lying and B and C are truthful, who is guilty?
questions.explanation: A is lying when he denies? Actually A says B guilty; with B truthful and guilty? This statement false if A guilty, so A liar. B says A guilty true, C says C innocent true. Thus A is guilty.

questions.q: Nine coins look identical, but one is lighter. In at most two weighings on a balance, how many coins can be narrowed by the first weighing?
questions.explanation: First weigh 3 versus3: if balanced, test remaining3; if unbalanced, test the lighter set of3.

questions.q: A triangle rotates 90° clockwise each step. After three such turns from its original position, the turn angle is:
questions.explanation: Three 90° rotations equal270° clockwise.

questions.q: The mirror image of P2 written horizontally with a vertical mirror reverses the sequence. Which is the mirror result?
questions.explanation: A vertical mirror reverses left-right order, so P2 becomes2P.

questions.q: A square is folded vertically and a circular hole is punched 1 cm from the folded edge. When unfolded, how many holes appear?
questions.explanation: A vertical fold doubles points on one side, producing two symmetric holes.

questions.q: A dot moves one position clockwise around a square at each step. From top-left, after four moves it is at:
questions.explanation: Four clockwise moves around a square return to the starting corner.

questions.q: Which shape is odd: circle, ellipse, spiral, line segment?
questions.explanation: Circle, ellipse and spiral are curved patterns, while a line segment is straight.

questions.q: A invests ₹18,000 for 8 months and B invests ₹24,000 for 6 months. Profit share ratio is:
questions.explanation: Capital-time products are 18,000×8=144,000 and24,000×6=144,000.

questions.q: Six years ago, A was twice B’s age. Today the sum of their ages is 45. B’s present age is:
questions.explanation: Let B today=b and A=45-b. Six years ago:39-b=2(b-6), so39-b=2b-12 and b=17.

questions.q: In a group of 80, 50 read X and 45 read Y. 30 read both. How many read neither?
How many 4-digit arrangements use 1,2,3,4 exactly once?
questions.explanation: A permutation of4 distinct digits has4!=24 arrangements.

questions.q: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. If two are drawn, probability both are red is:
